ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in the right triangle $ABC$, both quadrilaterals $DBFE$ and $GFIH$ are squares. Given that $AD=1\text{cm}$ and $DB=3\text{cm}$, what is the area of the shaded part in $\text{cm}^2$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $BE$, $FH$,\\
$\because$ $S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot DE+\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot EF$,\\
$\therefore$ $4BC=12+3BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=12$,\\
$\therefore$ $FC=BC-BF=12-3=9$,\\
$\because$ $S_{\triangle EFC}=\frac{1}{2}EF\cdot FC=\frac{1}{2}EF\cdot GH+\frac{1}{2}FC\cdot HI$,\\
$\therefore$ $27=3GH+9HI$,\\
$\therefore$ $GH=\frac{9}{4}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of square GFIH is: $\boxed{\frac{81}{16}}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in the right triangle $ABC$, both quadrilaterals $DBFE$ and $GFIH$ are squares. Given that $AD=1\text{cm}$ and $DB=3\text{cm}$, what is the area of the shaded part in $\text{cm}^2$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} As shown in the figure, connect $BE$, $FH$,\\
$\because$ $S_{\triangle ABC}=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot BC=\frac{1}{2}AB\cdot DE+\frac{1}{2}BC\cdot EF$,\\
$\therefore$ $4BC=12+3BC$,\\
$\therefore$ $BC=12$,\\
$\therefore$ $FC=BC-BF=12-3=9$,\\
$\because$ $S_{\triangle EFC}=\frac{1}{2}EF\cdot FC=\frac{1}{2}EF\cdot GH+\frac{1}{2}FC\cdot HI$,\\
$\therefore$ $27=3GH+9HI$,\\
$\therefore$ $GH=\frac{9}{4}$,\\
$\therefore$ the area of square $GFIH$ is $\boxed{\frac{81}{16}}$.
raw_record.final_cot:
Image description: In the figure, the right angle of right triangle ABC is at B, AB is vertical, BC is horizontal, A is above B, C is to the right of B, and AC is the hypotenuse. D is on AB, quadrilateral DBFE is a square, and E is on hypotenuse AC. Another smaller shaded square GFIH is located to the right of DBFE, F is its lower-left vertex, G is its upper-left vertex, I is its lower-right vertex, H is its upper-right vertex, and H is also on hypotenuse AC.
Reasoning: By the coordinate method, take B=(0,0), AB as the y-axis, and BC as the x-axis. It is known that AD=1 and DB=3, so AB=4, hence A=(0,4), D=(0,3). Because DBFE is a square, with side length DB=3, F=(3,0), E=(3,3). From the figure, E is on hypotenuse AC, so line AC passes through A=(0,4) and E=(3,3). Its slope is (3-4)/(3-0)=-1/3, so the equation of the line is y=4-x/3. Let y=0, obtaining x=12, therefore C=(12,0), BC=12.
Let the side length of the shaded square GFIH be s. From the position in the figure, F=(3,0), G=(3,s), I=(3+s,0), H=(3+s,s). Since H is on hypotenuse AC, substitute into y=4-x/3 to get s=4-(3+s)/3=3-s/3. Thus (4/3)s=3, s=9/4. The area of the shaded square is s^2=(9/4)^2=81/16.
